reference_traces.rationale: The reviewer identifies the TA-mediated thermo-reversible paste-to-gel composite as the central contribution; the final paper specifies the competitive TA–clay–PNIPAM network and reversible transition.

One reviewer disputed the degree of advance. The final paper positions the work as a previously unstudied paste-to-gel host–guest system, but this positioning does not itself resolve that scope-relative novelty disagreement.

The reviewer describes the regulated ternary interactions and reversible phase behavior; the final paper supplies the clay-free control showing that TA–PNIPAM alone does not form a paste-like network.
The reviewer identifies the thermally controlled paste/gel, self-healing, and deformation behavior; the final paper reports reversible modulus-state switching and cyclic recovery.

The reviewer questioned what the FTIR evidence establishes. The final paper presents the added TA-associated peak as only probably arising from the proposed interactions, leaving the molecular assignment qualified.

The reviewer requested a smaller-cavity macrocycle control. The final paper compares TA with larger-cavity BTA and nonmacrocyclic molecules, but does not provide the requested smaller-cavity macrocycle comparison.

The reviewer requested conventional mechanical comparison of the two systems. The final paper describes a tensile-test protocol, while its principal comparative evidence remains rheological, leaving the requested explicit paste/gel conventional-mechanics comparison unclear.

The reviewer asked for conductivity without the graphene-derived filler. The final paper presents the conductive formulation with sulfonated reduced graphene oxide and its circuit demonstration, leaving the baseline unfilled-system conductivity unreported in the final-paper evidence.

The reviewer questioned the 25 °C, 20 h polymerization and possible exotherm-related phase behavior. The final methods retain those conditions, so the experimental rationale and temperature-history evidence remain a residual reproducibility question.

The reviewer asked about effects substantially above 40 °C. The final paper records thermal measurements over 20–50 °C and reports temperature-dependent switching, but does not provide a focused account of side effects at higher temperatures.
Audit-only: the originally missing formulation range and hydration conditions were addressed in the response and are reflected in the final composition and testing-method spans.
Audit-only: the requested clay-free control and clarified substitute-molecule conditions were added; final-paper controls support the resolution.
Audit-only: contextual literature, clay structural information, and the DLS-distribution explanation were added or clarified in the final state.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Calibrate the novelty claim against the closest prior dynamic hydrogel and host–guest systems, specifying the technical distinction demonstrated here.
limiting_points.text: Novelty remains contested: the manuscript frames competitive host–guest paste-to-gel transitions as previously unstudied, whereas one reviewer did not view the advance as sufficiently distinctive in context.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Retain a precise comparison between the binary PNIPAM–clay gel and the TA-containing ternary paste-to-gel system.
supporting_points.text: The specific claimed advance is a protonated-TA, clay, and PNIPAM ternary network that couples competitive interactions to a reversible, thermally triggered paste-to-gel transition.

questions.suggested_action: Report polymerization-time conversion or network-development data and record the reaction temperature profile under the stated formulation.
questions.text: What direct evidence establishes that 20 h at 25 °C is required for this formulation, and that polymerization heat does not induce inhomogeneity or an unintended PNIPAM transition?

questions.suggested_action: Quantify reversibility, morphology, and mechanical retention across an expanded high-temperature range and state any degradation threshold.
questions.text: How do repeated exposures above the reported switching window affect phase reversibility, water loss, and the material’s mechanical or self-healing behavior?

strengths.suggested_action: Keep the clay-free and nonmacrocyclic controls prominent when presenting the ternary-network mechanism.
strengths.text: The study distinguishes the roles of the three components: clay is necessary for a cohesive network, while the TA cavity is contrasted with nonmacrocyclic controls and larger-cavity BTA.

strengths.suggested_action: Present the reversible rheology and cyclic recovery alongside the operational temperature range.
strengths.text: The final paper provides a coherent functional package linking thermally reversible modulus-state switching with cyclic strain recovery of the TA-containing paste.

summary.text: The paper reports a TA–clay–PNIPAM supramolecular paste whose competitive interactions are proposed to enable reversible thermal switching between a moldable paste and a more rigid gel, with accompanying self-healing and conductive-filler demonstrations. The final state adds composition, control, and mechanistic material, while the remaining review focus is the strength of molecular assignment, the completeness of cavity-size and mechanics controls, conductivity baselines, and high-temperature/polymerization characterization.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Add hydrated-state or orthogonal spectroscopic evidence with quantitative analysis that discriminates the proposed TA–PNIPAM and TA–clay interactions.
weaknesses.text: The spectroscopic support for the proposed interaction network remains qualified: the final FTIR discussion attributes the added TA-associated feature only probabilistically, so FTIR alone does not fully establish the claimed binding changes.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Test a smaller-cavity macrocycle, or explicitly limit the cavity-size conclusion to the available TA, BTA, and nonmacrocyclic comparisons.
weaknesses.text: The cavity-size argument is bounded by the available controls: larger-cavity BTA and nonmacrocyclic molecules are tested, but a smaller-cavity macrocycle is not.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Identify the samples used in tensile testing and provide an explicit conventional-mechanics comparison of the accessible paste and gel states, with its temperature and hydration conditions.
weaknesses.text: Mechanical comparison is primarily rheological; the final methods describe tensile testing but do not make an explicit conventional-mechanics comparison of the PNIPAM–clay gel and the thermally switched TA-containing material clear.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Report conductivity and circuit performance for the unfilled paste and quantify the incremental effect of sulfonated reduced graphene oxide.
weaknesses.text: The electrical demonstration establishes function for the sulfonated-rGO-filled paste, but does not isolate the baseline electrical behavior of the water-containing unfilled paste.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: Resolved audit item: formulation variation, solid-content information, and the native hydration condition are documented in the final state.
Resolved audit item: the clay-free comparator and same-condition substitute-molecule controls are represented in the final paper.
Resolved audit item: the introduction context, clay description, and DLS-distribution explanation are present in the final state.
